newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania replaces top-echelon army officers.
newsitem.headline: Romania replaces top-echelon army officers.

text.p: Romania's new civilian defence minister replaced two top generals on Thursday, including the army's chief of staff, as part of "democratic moves", the Defence Ministry said.
Minister Victor Babiuc released General Dumitru Cioflina from his job as secretary of state and army chief of staff, appointing General Constantin Degeratu to replace him, a ministry statement said.

General Dan Zaharia was appointed secretary of state and head of the army's procurement department, replacing General Florentin Popa. Defence officials said the moves were "part of Romania's strides to democracy".

Babiuc, who took over the defence job in the new centrist coalition government which replaced leftists after last November's elections, has pledged to step up policy efforts aimed at gaining Romania early admission into NATO.
"The practice of all democratic states is to periodically change (the jobs of) top-echelon army officers," government spokesman Eugen Serbanescu said, commenting on the move.
Both Cioflina and Popa would soon be assigned "to other top missions," he said, without elaborating.
After the 1989 collapse of communism, the military underwent sweeping reforms which spearheaded Romania's drive to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation as a full member.
In 1993 Romania was the first ex-communist eastern European country to sign up for NATO's Partnership for Peace scheme, aimed at strenghtening military ties with former Cold War foes.
NATO military leaders have praised the Balkan country for its active role within the partnership programme.
